rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.3, 3.4, Table 7 and Figure 9 - the authors collected 84 topsoil samples (July 2021) in the Ogan-Kucha River Oasis, Xinjiang, measured EC 1:5 in the laboratory, built PLSR models from PlanetScope bands and new yellow/red-edge salinity indices, and produced 3-m soil EC maps (XGBoost-PLSR R2v 0.832, RMSEv 12.05, RPD 2.44).
rows.notes: The study's own result is that PlanetScope imagery with newly built yellow-band and red-edge salinity indices can estimate and map topsoil salinity (EC) at 3-m resolution with good validation accuracy in one arid oasis. It shows remote sensing detecting/mapping a soil degradation hazard (salinity), not remote sensing supporting soil management or maintaining soil quality; no management action or soil-quality outcome is tested. This is a precondition of the claimed effect, so Q2 is 'no' and upstream is set. Had the claim been about salinity monitoring, the study would have given Q8 'yes' (Section 4.4: single date, no time series, interference from texture, vegetation and moisture, limited spectral bands) and Q9 arguably 'no' (only RMSE/R2/RPD, no dispersion of the mapped result).

notes: Full text appears complete (abstract through references), with some duplicated/overlapping lines from PDF extraction at page boundaries. Minor internal inconsistencies in the paper (training/validation set sizes 58/26 vs 59/25; correlation coefficients labelled R2) do not affect the rating.
